nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Daily 6:00 AM server time. Mirrors the Phase-1 Google Sheets reporting agent cadence.

nodes.name: Sync Now Webhook
nodes.notes: Called by the dashboard 'Sync Now' button (DashboardLayout.tsx -> triggerSyncNow). Responds immediately (onReceived); the dashboard reloads its data a few seconds later, best-effort.

nodes.name: Get all campaigns
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData: an empty campaigns table must not halt the whole workflow (incl. the discovery branch). Downstream nodes skip rows with no meta_campaign_id.

nodes.name: Filter synced campaigns
nodes.notes: One item per campaign that has actually been built on Meta (meta_campaign_id set). The rest of the metric/recommendation/config chain processes each independently.

nodes.name: Fetch insights
nodes.notes: Meta returns { data: [] } for a campaign with no spend yesterday — that is normal, not an error. 'Build metrics row' falls back to a zero row so daily history stays gap-free.

nodes.name: Delete existing metrics row
nodes.notes: Delete-then-insert = idempotent re-runs (unique(campaign_id,date)). alwaysOutputData: zero rows deleted (normal first run) must not halt the branch.

nodes.name: Fetch recommendations
nodes.notes: Meta's `recommendations` edge is thin compared to Google's — it returns { recommendations: [{ code, title, message, confidence, importance, blame_field }] } when present and omits the field entirely otherwise. No dollar impact is provided, so dollars_recoverable is left null. If your app/token can't read this field it just comes back empty; that's fine.

nodes.name: Delete existing open recommendations
nodes.notes: Clears previously-open recs so ones Meta no longer surfaces stop showing. Does NOT touch applied/dismissed rows.

nodes.name: Fetch campaign config
nodes.notes: campaign.daily_budget is only set for Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) campaigns; otherwise budget lives on the ad set. 'Reconcile config' also fetches the ad set budget when meta_adset_id is present.

parameters.url: ={{ $('Filter synced campaigns').item.json.metaAdsetId ? ('https://graph.facebook.com/v21.0/' + $('Filter synced campaigns').item.json.metaAdsetId) : ('https://graph.facebook.com/v21.0/' + $('Filter synced campaigns').item.json.metaCampaignId + '/adsets') }}

nodes.name: Fetch adset budget
nodes.notes: When meta_adset_id is already known, fetches that ad set directly (returns a plain object). When it's missing (e.g. a discovered campaign we never captured the ad set id for), falls back to the campaign's /adsets edge instead (returns { data: [...] }) and picks the first one — this is also how meta_adset_id gets backfilled, in 'Reconcile config'. 'limit' is ignored (harmlessly) on the direct-object call.

nodes.name: Reconcile config
nodes.notes: Reconciles campaigns.status + daily_budget_usd + meta_adset_id + targeting to whatever Meta actually reports — catches changes made directly in Ads Manager, and self-heals campaigns discovered before we captured their ad set (meta_adset_id was null, so budget/targeting stayed blank forever until this ran). Does NOT touch pending_review (a build-time / launch-decision concept, not something Meta knows about).

nodes.name: Wait for recommendations
nodes.notes: Pure synchronization barrier — 'Build suggestion context' reads $('Build recommendation items').all() by name, but that node lives on a parallel branch with no other connection back to this one. Without this Merge, n8n can run 'Build suggestion context' before 'Build recommendation items' has finished, throwing "Node ... hasn't been executed" (confirmed live) — same root cause as the 'Wait For All Fetches' fix in the Phase-1 reporting agent. The merged output itself isn't used; Build suggestion context still reads every source by name.

options.systemMessage:
You are reviewing this Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Ads campaign's daily performance sync automatically, on behalf of an agency, with no human having asked a question. Decide whether there's a genuinely useful, specific, non-obvious suggestion worth surfacing right now — a clear problem (real spend with zero results, runaway cost per result, obvious frequency/fatigue issue) or a binding budget. Be conservative: should_post = false unless something actually stands out. A missed suggestion beats noise the agency learns to ignore.

When should_post is true, action_type follows the same rules as everywhere in this project: "none" UNLESS you're suggesting exactly one of update_daily_budget (daily_budget_usd required, a specific positive number), pause_campaign, or resume_campaign, with a one-sentence reason in the reason field. For action_type "none" (most posts), set daily_budget_usd to 0 and reason to an empty string.

nodes.name: Gemini Chat Model
nodes.notes: Swapped from OpenAI (org ran out of credits, confirmed live 2026-09-15). Reuses the existing 'Google Gemini(PaLM) Api account' credential. modelName is a guess at a currently-available Gemini model — pick from the node's own live model dropdown if this one doesn't resolve.

nodes.name: Insert proactive suggestion
nodes.notes: Posts into the same campaign_chat_messages table the Campaign Assistant tab reads — shows up like an unprompted assistant message. Confirm & Apply / Dismiss work identically.

nodes.name: Get owned ad accounts
nodes.notes: Lists real ad accounts under the Business Manager. Add client_ad_accounts too if you also manage accounts owned by clients' own businesses and shared to yours (GET /{bm}/client_ad_accounts).

nodes.name: Resolve accounts to clients
nodes.notes: One item per ad account that maps to exactly one client (clients.meta_ad_account_id). Ambiguous or unclaimed accounts are skipped rather than guessed — the same failure mode the Google Ads sibling hit live.

nodes.name: Filter new campaigns
nodes.notes: Index-matches each account's campaign list back to its client. primary_goal / business_objective are left null — those are intake concepts that don't apply to a campaign discovered rather than built here (schema allows null).

nodes.name: Insert discovered campaign
nodes.notes: pending_review=false — a campaign that already existed on Meta was never 'awaiting the agency's launch decision'. continueOnFail: a unique(meta_campaign_id) conflict from a race just skips that one row.
